newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea physical crude markets muted by surging pape.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea physical crude markets muted by surging pape.

text.p: Wet Brent settled in the middle of Friday's trading range on Monday, with the physical market overshadowed by a surge in IPE Brent futures, traders said.
Two Brent cargoes, one loading Jan 17-19 and one Jan 18-20 traded at Feb Brent +16 cents, four cents down on Friday's highest traded levels but six cents up on the lowest.
The sole Brent date nominated from the paper chains on Monday was kept by trading house Arcadia.
Feb Brent paper climbed 50 cents in line with IPE futures at $24.62 a barrel by 1845 GMT.
Spreads regained some strength after modest early losses.
Feb/March traded at +51 cents and +52 cents. Jan/Feb was rumoured to have traded earlier at +20 cents, and was talked later at +18/+24 cents, with March/April steady at +57/60 cents.
CFDs for this week roared higher to a peak of Feb Brent +13 cents. Next week's levels were pegged at Feb +2/+8 cents.
Activity on other North sea grades was quiet, although a third decade Oseberg cargo was rumoured traded at a higher number than Friday.
A European major was seen offering three or four third decade Forties cargoes but nothing was heard moved by late in the day.
"Nothing is moving, they're just watching the screen go up and up," said one trader.
With Italy and Spain on holiday there was little action on the Mediterranean sour market, although a cargo of Iraqi Kirkuk crude was heard offered into northwest Europe at Dated Brent -60 cents.
Traders said that Russian Urals was well supplied though most did not expect to see a further drop in the differentials.
Urals was assessed around Dated Brent -$1.10 a barrel. The cargo bought by a refiner on Friday at Dated -$1.15 was done on a c+f Med basis.
